TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Banda Sea
DATE 24 November 2028 · 0610 local
SIDE People's Liberation Army Navy
WINDOW 35 min, closes at 52
Arafura-class OPV (stand-in). Photo: VolgaDnper1488 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · cropped
"Stability is not a passive state of affairs - it's achieved through strength and active diplomacy."
- Air Marshal Robert Chipman, Chief of Air Force, RAAF, 2023

BANDA SEA, 0610. At 0447 FLYING SHARK 85, a J-15 on LIAONING's dawn patrol, reported a fire warning sixty miles south-east of the group and went into the sea at 0452. The pilot ejected. His beacon has been transmitting since 0455, and he is on your plot, alive in his raft.

The Australians heard it too. A patrol vessel of theirs in the southern approaches turned for the beacon at 0540 and is closing at about twenty knots, a little under nine miles off him. Nobody aboard her has fired at anybody. Anything that happens to her, or to the Poseidon overhead, is the group firing on a ship that is recovering a man.

Your detachment is about seven miles north-west of him: closer than she is, and faster. Short of your best speed she is there first. Get the lead ship close alongside, inside three cables, stopped, put the boat in the water and hold there until he is aboard: about four minutes. If the patrol vessel is alongside him first, he goes home on the Australians' timetable, and the coalition has a photograph of a Chinese pilot on an Australian deck.
Your ships and the ship's flight start at weapons Hold. Two Banda fishing boats are on the water.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.
Fleet headquarters
COMMANDER'S INTENT

A pilot of the group's is alive in the water, and the coalition can hear his beacon as well as we can. He comes home in a Chinese ship. Get there first and get him aboard, and fire on nothing to do it: whatever yesterday was, this morning is a man in the water. The patrol vessel is doing what any ship does for one. Do not stop her from doing it, and do not let her be the one who does.
• Get the lead ship alongside the pilot and hold there until he is aboard, before the patrol vessel reaches him
• Fire on nothing: not the patrol vessel, not the aircraft
• Classify the patrol vessel and the aircraft over her
• Harm no fishing boat

Your detachment, with the ship's flight if one is embarked. In the water: the pilot of Flying Shark 85, in his raft. Racing you: an Australian patrol vessel. Watching: a RAAF P-8A. Neutral: two fishing boats.

The planned window is 35 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 17 minutes more; the operation is closed at 52 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
